translations.answer: In the GMR paper, the ground penetration, self-collision, and joint jumps in specific actions significantly reduce the policy success rate or increase tracking errors in the Unitree G1, 21 LAFAN1 action sequences and unified BeyondMimic training setup. The GMR approach with root translation uniform scaling, local/non-uniform scaling of the body, and two-stage IK outperforms the open-source re-targeting of PHC/ProtoMotions, but this conclusion has not been verified for other robots, object interactions, or real-world randomized trials.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: Human motion is converted into a robot joint/reference trajectory before tracker training.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: The downstream policy is trained with the same BeyondMimic setup so retargeting is the principal varied factor.
translations.applicability.assumptions.2: Reference motions do not require sustained object or environment interaction.
translations.applicability.environments.1: noise/model/latency perturbations used by the paper
translations.applicability.robots.0: Unitree G1 in the paper evaluation
translations.confidence_rationale: The paper isolates retargeting across a shared tracker and reports per-motion failures, large repeated-trial evaluations, tracking errors, and identifiable artifacts. The official commit exposes the scaling and two-stage IK implementation. Confidence is capped because the study uses one robot, one motion dataset, no object interactions, and no randomized real-robot comparison.
translations.evidence.0.locator: Equations 2-6, Figure 2, Table I, Table II, Figure 3, and Table III
translations.evidence.0.note: Connects scaling and two-stage IK design to downstream success/error and identifies penetration, self-intersection, joint jumps, and start-frame sensitivity.
translations.evidence.0.title: Retargeting Matters: General Motion Retargeting for Humanoid Motion Tracking
